# s3dol

s3 (through boto3) with a simple (dict-like or list-like) interface

To install:	`pip install s3dol`

[Documentation](https://i2mint.github.io/s3dol/)

## Quick start

```python
import s3dol

s = s3dol.s3_store("my-bucket")  # MutableMapping[str, bytes]
s["hello.txt"] = b"world"
s["hello.txt"]  # b'world'
list(s)
"hello.txt" in s
del s["hello.txt"]

s = s3dol.s3_store("my-bucket", prefix="logs/")  # scoped to a prefix
s = s3dol.s3_store("open-data", anon=True)  # public bucket, no credentials
s = s3dol.s3_store("b", preset="minio", endpoint_url="http://localhost:9000")
```

Starting from nothing (the default never creates a bucket from a typo):

```python
s = s3dol.s3_store("brand-new-bucket", on_missing_bucket="create")
```

**Big objects go through the same interface** — no `upload_multipart` method:

```python
s["video.mp4"] = s3dol.Filepath("/tmp/video.mp4")  # streamed, multipart above 8 MiB
s["stream.bin"] = s3dol.Chunks(chunk_iterator)  # never fully in memory
```

**Keyed capabilities are stores you index**, not methods (a `dol` key wrapper
hands a method the *unmapped* key — so s3dol has none):

```python
s3dol.handles(s)["video.mp4"].read(offset=0, length=1024)  # ranged read
s3dol.handles(s)["video.mp4"].url(expires_in=3600)  # presigned URL
s3dol.urls(s)["video.mp4"]  # ...or directly
s3dol.info(s)["video.mp4"].size  # one HeadObject
```

Everything else is a free function taking the store first:

```python
s3dol.sub(s, "folder/")
s3dol.prefixes(s)
s3dol.delete_many(s, ["a", "b"])
s3dol.delete_bucket(endpoint, "name", force=True)
```

**Test without a cloud** — no network, no docker, no moto:

```python
from s3dol.testing import mock_s3, run_conformance


def test_my_service():
    assert MediaService(mock_s3(data={"a.mp4": b"..."})).play("a.mp4")
```

`run_conformance(make_store)` is exported too: run the same laws against your
own store (or a sibling `*dol` package’s).

## Heads-up: v1 is coming — run `s3dol.diagnose()` now

A major, behaviour-clarifying v1 is in progress
(design: [`misc/docs/architecture.md`]() and the ADRs in
[`misc/docs/decisions/`]()). Today’s `S3Store` will keep
working through a compatibility shim, but a few v0 behaviours were bugs
(e.g. an explicit `endpoint_url=` being silently dropped whenever
`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` are exported) and v1 fixes them —
which can *move where your data goes*.

Before upgrading to v1, run the diagnosis with the same arguments you pass
`S3Store` today, in the environment you deploy in:

```python
import s3dol

s3dol.diagnose(bucket_name="my-bucket", endpoint_url="...", path="...")
```

It prints what resolves (endpoint, region, signing, credential *source* — never
a secret), where each value came from, and a **v0-vs-v1 divergence table**
telling you whether the upgrade changes anything for your call. It never
raises; a failing resolution is part of the report.

## Set up credentials

Recommended prerequisite to make getting started easier but not required.

### Option 1: [Environment Variables](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-envvars.html)

```default
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-west-2
```

### Option 2: [Configure Default Profile in Credentials File](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-files.html)

Add credentails in `~/.aws/credentials`

```default
[default]
aws_access_key_id = AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
aws_secret_access_key = wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
```

### Option 3: [Configure Default Profile with AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/configure/)

[Install AWS CLI](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html)

```bash
brew instal awscli
```

Set credentails with CLI

```bash
aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
Default region name [None]: us-west-2
Default output format [None]:
```

# _autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md

# s3dol.base

Layer B — close-to-metal stores over one bucket or one endpoint.

Design record: `misc/docs/architecture.md` (the contract tables) on
ADR-0001 (layering; the prefix lives HERE, in the leaf), ADR-0004 (one error
seam), ADR-0005 (write domain / strategies), ADR-0006 (prefix arithmetic and
key validity), ADR-0008 (`__len__` absent by design), ADR-0010 (bucket policy),
ADR-0011 (**no key-taking public methods** — one guarded exception, `url_for`),
ADR-0012 (connection).

The class triads mirror `dol.filesys` and `azuredol`:

```default
BucketCollection   -> BucketReader   -> BucketStore     (keys: object keys)
EndpointCollection -> EndpointReader -> EndpointStore   (keys: bucket names)
ObjectHandle                                            (not a Mapping)
```

Reader-only classes are *real classes* (a type checker catches
`reader[k] = v`; a read-scoped credential never even attempts a write) —
`dol.mk_read_only` is non-functional on a dol store (verified, ADR-0001).

**The rule for what may join a class here: nothing that takes a key**
(ADR-0011 D1). `dol` wrappers hand any non-dunder method the outer, unmapped
key, and the standard escape (`wrapped_self`) is itself silently wrong when
nothing references the wrapper. Keyed capabilities are sibling stores
(`s3dol.handles(store)[k]` — `capabilities.py`); per-object richness lives on
[`ObjectHandle`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.ObjectHandle) (key bound at construction); everything else is a free
function taking the store first. The single exception is
[`BucketReader.url_for()`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketReader.url_for), kept for `dol.SupportsUrlFor`, guarded to be
correct-or-loud (D3b). A reflective conformance test enforces the rule (D5).

### *class* s3dol.base.BucketReader(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

+ `__getitem__` -> bytes (or the read strategy’s value type).

#### url_for(k, , expires_in=3600, client_method='get_object', \*\*params)

Presigned URL for `k` — **the one keyed method** (ADR-0011 D3b),
kept solely because `dol.SupportsUrlFor` requires a *method* and
`dol.content_url` reaches it by `getattr`. The canonical form is
`s3dol.urls(store)[k]`.

Guarded to be correct-or-loud, never silently wrong:

- **unwrapped store**: `k` is a key in this store’s own key space,
  so the URL addresses `self._id_of_key(k)`. Correct, and this is
  also the contract `dol.content_url` calls under — it resolves the
  key through the *outer* layers and stops at the layer owning
  `url_for`, “because that layer applies its own”
  (`dol/content.py`);
- **this leaf has ever been wrapped**: **raises**. Two call paths then
  reach this one signature with *different key domains* and nothing
  distinguishes them: `dol.content_url` hands over a key already
  mapped through the wrapper layers, while a direct
  `wrapped.url_for(k)` (delegation) hands over the raw outer key.
  Applying `_id_of_key` is right for the first and wrong for the
  second; re-resolving through the chain is right for the second and
  double-transforms the first. Since a wrong presigned URL addresses a
  *different real object*, the only honest answer is refusal, naming
  the sibling store — which is correct by construction because it goes
  through `__getitem__` (ADR-0011 D2/D3b, and see the note below);
- **anonymous connection**: returns `None` (`SupportsUrlFor` is
  `Optional[str]`; raising would turn a public-bucket streaming
  fallback into a 500 — ADR-0012 D5). The check reads the built
  client’s signature version, never `spec.anon`.

#### NOTE
This refusal is a *finding*, not a limitation we chose.
ADR-0011 D3b expected a guarded method to serve both paths; it
cannot, on a leaf that owns its prefix. Reported upstream on
dol#86/#83 as evidence that a keyed capability *method* is
unfixable in the general case, and that the sibling-store form is
the only one correct by construction.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### *class* s3dol.base.BucketStore(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketReader`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketReader), `KvPersister`

+ `__setitem__` / `__delitem__`. The user-facing read-write store.

#### pop(k) → v, remove specified key and return the corresponding value.

If key is not found, d is returned if given, otherwise KeyError is raised.

#### setdefault(k) → D.get(k,d), also set D[k]=d if k not in D

#### update(other=(), , \*\*kwargs)

If E present and has a .keys() method, does:     for k in E.keys(): D[k] = E[k]
If E present and lacks .keys() method, does:     for (k, v) in E: D[k] = v
In either case, this is followed by: for k, v in F.items(): D[k] = v

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

# _autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md

# s3dol.capabilities

Keyed capabilities as sibling stores; non-keyed operations as free
functions (ADR-0011 D2/D3/D4).

A keyed capability is a Layer B `KvReader` over the **same key space** whose
`__getitem__` returns the capability:

```default
BucketStore                     k -> bytes
BucketHandles  s3dol.handles(s) k -> ObjectHandle
BucketUrls     s3dol.urls(s)    k -> presigned URL (str) | None
BucketInfo     s3dol.info(s)    k -> ObjectInfo (one HeadObject per key)
BucketListedInfo  s3dol.listed_info(s)  k -> ObjectInfo (one LIST, a snapshot)
```

`__getitem__` is the one thing `dol` maps correctly at every wrapper depth,
so sibling stores are correct *by construction*: no `inner_most_key`, no
`wrapped_self`, no guard — immune to both the lost-reference hole (D1a) and
the non-`Store`-layer hole (D3a), the only form in ADR-0011 that is.

**The cost, stated plainly** (D2): a user who wraps the data store must wrap
the sibling in parallel:

```default
s = s3_store('bucket', prefix='p/')
h = s3dol.handles(s)
c = KeyCodecs.prefixed('x/')      # a user-applied key codec
s2, h2 = c(s), c(h)               # wrap BOTH
h2['f']                           # -> handle on 'p/x/f'; correct at any depth
```

The accessors therefore derive a sibling from an **unwrapped** store and
**raise** on a wrapped one, naming that remedy — s3dol will not guess a user’s
codec chain (that is dol#10).

Free functions (D3) resolve keys with the store held as an argument (alive, so
no weakref registry is consulted). Per D3a they are *more* reliable than
methods, not reliable: a hand-rolled non-`Store` passthrough layer in the
chain can still defeat the resolution — no docstring here claims “correct at
any wrapper depth”; only the sibling stores may claim that.

| [`DELETE_MANY_CHUNK`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.DELETE_MANY_CHUNK)   | AWS's DeleteObjects cap.   |

### *class* s3dol.capabilities.BucketHandles(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

`k -> ObjectHandle` (key bound at construction; zero round-trips).

### *class* s3dol.capabilities.BucketInfo(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

`k -> ObjectInfo` (one `HeadObject`).

### *class* s3dol.capabilities.BucketListedInfo(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

`k -> ObjectInfo` from the listing rows, not one `HeadObject` per key.

The first access (a lookup or an iteration) pages through `ListObjectsV2`
once and keeps `{key: ObjectInfo}` (`size`, `last_modified`, `etag`,
`storage_class`; `content_type` and the other HEAD-only fields stay
`None`). It is **lazy and a snapshot**: later writes are not seen; make a
new `listed_info(store)` to refresh. A whole-bucket ETag comparison costs
one LIST per 1000 keys.

### *class* s3dol.capabilities.BucketUrls(\*args, expires_in=3600, client_method='get_object', \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

`k -> presigned URL` (zero object requests; `None` when anonymous).
The canonical spelling of what `url_for` shims (ADR-0011 D3b).

### s3dol.capabilities.DELETE_MANY_CHUNK *= 1000*

AWS’s DeleteObjects cap. moto accepts 1001, so tier 2 can never catch a
missing chunker (ADR-0010 §2) — hence the constant is also unit-tested.

### s3dol.capabilities.delete_bucket(endpoint, name, , force=False)

Delete bucket `name`. Refuses a non-empty bucket unless
`force=True`, in which case the cascade **paginates** — v0 listed one
page, deleted ≤1000 objects, then failed: a partial, non-idempotent
destruction (ADR-0010 §3). A free function, not a method (ADR-0011 D4).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### s3dol.capabilities.delete_many(store, keys)

Bulk delete (ADR-0010 §2; a free function per ADR-0011 D4 — keyed +
destructive + delegated is the census’s data-destroying shape).

Chunks at 1000 (AWS’s cap), parses the `Errors` list out of the HTTP
200 response, and on partial failure raises one `S3PartialFailure`
carrying `.succeeded` and `.failures`. Absent keys are reported by S3
as `Deleted` — this function does **not** distinguish them (same
idempotency as `del store[k]`).

Keys are the *caller’s* keys: with the store held as an argument the
chain is resolved via `dol.inner_most_key` (alive store — no weakref
hole). Validate-the-target caveat (D4): the first argument must be an
s3dol store or a dol wrapper over one.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### s3dol.capabilities.handles(store)

The sibling store of `ObjectHandle`s: `handles(s)[k]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketHandles`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketHandles)

### s3dol.capabilities.info(store)

The sibling store of `ObjectInfo`: `info(s)[k]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketInfo)

### s3dol.capabilities.listed_info(store)

The sibling store of `ObjectInfo` built from one paginated LIST:
`listed_info(s)[k]` (a lazy snapshot; see [`BucketListedInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketListedInfo)).

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketListedInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketListedInfo)

### s3dol.capabilities.prefixes(store)

The ‘directories’ one level under the store’s scope, \*\*relative to the
caller’s key space\*\* — one `ListObjectsV2(Delimiter='/')` reading
`CommonPrefixes` (which v0 parsed and then called from nowhere;
ADR-0009). Through a dol wrapper chain, the listing is rooted at the
caller’s scope (each prefix layer’s contribution) and results are mapped
back **outward** (`_key_of_id` per layer, innermost first — the inverse
walk `dol` does not provide; ADR-0011 D3). A wrapper whose codec cannot
express the scope raises — loud, not wrong.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### s3dol.capabilities.sub(store, prefix)

A store scoped to `prefix`, **in the caller’s key space** (D3).

Two branches, deliberately different (each documented in the ADR):

- **unwrapped s3dol store**: `leaf._with(prefix=...)` — cheap, keeps
  server-side prefix pushdown, returns the same class;
- **dol-wrapped store**: composes `Pipe(filt_iter.prefixes(p),
  KeyCodecs.prefixed(p))` over the *outer* store (filter FIRST — the only
  safe composition, ADR-0006 §1), which preserves the user’s codecs but
  loses pushdown (a full scan filtered client-side; D8 closed this: the
  cheap path is the unwrapped branch) and returns a different type.

### s3dol.capabilities.urls(store, , expires_in=3600, client_method='get_object')

The sibling store of presigned URLs: `urls(s)[k]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketUrls`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketUrls)


# _autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md

# s3dol.connection

`S3Connection` — the credential + endpoint SSOT, and the pure resolver.

Design record: `misc/docs/decisions/0012-credential-and-endpoint-resolution.md`
(all of it) on top of `0002-boto3-as-engine.md` (lazy boto3) and
`0003-provider-presets-and-capabilities.md` (presets, SigV4 mandate).

The two sentences the module follows from (ADR-0012):

1. **A preset is the caller’s explicit endpoint, spelled by name.** It sits
   exactly where `endpoint_url=` sits — above every environment and
   config-file channel. s3dol owns two rungs of the endpoint ladder, not six.
2. \*\*A `Config` value s3dol does not set is a channel it leaves open to the
   user.\*\* Every field is a ladder with a documented bottom, and “the row makes
   no claim” is spelled by *omitting the key*, never by passing `None`.

Structure:

- [`S3Connection`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.S3Connection) — a frozen, picklable spec. No live objects, no
  escape hatch for one. Construction performs no I/O and imports no boto3.
- [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve) — a **pure** function `(spec, environ, aws_config) ->
  Resolution` where every field carries its provenance. Tier-1 tests cover
  the whole ladder with a fake environ dict and zero I/O.
- [`load_aws_config()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.load_aws_config) — the separate, *named impure* loader for the
  aws-config rungs; pass it (or its result) to [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve).
- Credential shapes (ADR-0012 D5) — normalised in `__post_init__` to small
  frozen, picklable providers; live botocore objects are rejected with
  shape-specific messages.

```pycon
>>> spec = S3Connection(endpoint_url='http://localhost:9000',
...                     credentials=('AKIAEXAMPLE', 'sEkR3tVALUE'))
>>> res = resolve(spec, {})
>>> res.endpoint_url.value, res.endpoint_url.source
('http://localhost:9000', 'endpoint_url=')
>>> res.signature_version.value  # never left to botocore (ADR-0003 §4)
's3v4'
>>> 'sEkR3tVALUE' in repr(spec)  # secrets never in repr (ADR-0012 D1)
False
```

### Functions

| [`load_aws_config`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.load_aws_config)()                    | The named, *impure* aws-config loader (ADR-0012 D2): loads the shared config via botocore (~16 ms — never on the common path; pass this function as a thunk and [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve) calls it only if a rung needs it), scrubbed of anything credential-shaped.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`normalize_credentials`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.normalize_credentials)(value)         | Normalise every accepted credential shape; reject the rest, each with its own message (ADR-0012 D5).                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`resolve`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve)(spec, environ[, aws_config]) | Pure resolution: no `os.environ`, no disk, no network (ADR-0012 D2).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Classes

| [`CallableCredentials`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.CallableCredentials)(fetch)                       | A picklable zero-arg callable returning a mapping with keys `access_key`/`secret_key` (aliases: `key`/`secret`), optional `token`, optional `expires_at`/`expiry_time` (ISO 8601).    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CredentialProvider`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.CredentialProvider)()                             | Base of s3dol's picklable credential specs.                                                                                                                                           |

| [`Resolution`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.Resolution)(endpoint_url, region_name, ...)       | The result of [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve) — everything `diagnose()` prints and everything client-build consumes.                                       |

| [`Sourced`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.Sourced)(value, source[, passed])                 | A resolved value, where it came from, and whether s3dol passes it to botocore explicitly (`passed=False` == the key is omitted so the channel below stays open — "omit, never None"). |
| [`StaticCredentials`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.StaticCredentials)(access_key, secret_key[, ...]) | An explicit key pair (optionally a session token).                                                                                                                                    |

### *class* s3dol.connection.CallableCredentials(fetch)

Bases: [`CredentialProvider`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.CredentialProvider)

A picklable zero-arg callable returning a mapping with keys
`access_key`/`secret_key` (aliases: `key`/`secret`), optional
`token`, optional `expires_at`/`expiry_time` (ISO 8601). With an
expiry, credentials are refreshable — the callable is re-invoked by
botocore’s refresh machinery (advisory 900 s / mandatory 600 s before
expiry).

#### provenance()

A label for diagnose() — never a credential value.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### *class* s3dol.connection.CredentialProvider

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Base of s3dol’s picklable credential specs.

Subclasses are small frozen dataclasses that *describe* how to obtain
credentials; nothing live is held (nothing live pickles — measured, ADR-0012
D5). At client-build time each is adapted into a botocore provider and
**replaces** botocore’s resolver via
`session.register_component('credential_provider', ...)` — never
prepended (silent fallthrough) and never `insert_before` (raises when a
profile is set).

#### provenance()

A label for diagnose() — never a credential value.

everything client-build consumes. Carries provenance labels, never a

### *class* s3dol.connection.S3Connection(preset=None, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, profile=None, credentials=None, anon=False, signature_version='s3v4', addressing_style=None, checksum=None, payload_signing_enabled=None, verify=None, client_kwargs=(), deny_means_absent=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A frozen, picklable connection spec. No live objects — ever.

Construction performs no I/O and does not import boto3 (ADR-0002); the
client is built lazily, once, under a per-instance lock (CPython ≥3.12
removed `cached_property`’s lock deliberately — measured: 8 racing
threads → 8 clients without one).

`__post_init__` is the only door: every normalisation and contradiction
check happens here, so a bad shape dies at construction with a message,
not later inside botocore.

```pycon
>>> S3Connection(anon=True, profile='prod')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError: ...
```

#### *property* client

The boto3 S3 client — built lazily, once, under the lock.

#### *property* presign_client

The client presigned URLs are generated with.

For most providers this is [`client`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.S3Connection.client). Two providers genuinely
need different config for presigning than for the API (ADR-0003 §1):
Hetzner presigns virtual-hosted while the API is path-style; R2
presigns only on the S3 API domain. When the resolved preset carries
`presign_endpoint_url`/`presign_addressing_style`, a second client
is built (lazily, once, under the same lock) from the merged config.

#### resolution(environ=None, aws_config=<function load_aws_config>)

Resolve against the real environment by default (a thin impure
wrapper over the pure [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve)).

* **Return type:**
  [`Resolution`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.Resolution)

A resolved value, where it came from, and whether s3dol passes it to

An explicit key pair (optionally a session token).

#### NOTE
a *static* token expires and cannot refresh — prefer `profile=` or

#### provenance()

A label for diagnose() — never a credential value.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### s3dol.connection.load_aws_config()

The named, *impure* aws-config loader (ADR-0012 D2): loads the shared
config via botocore (~16 ms — never on the common path; pass this function
as a thunk and [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.resolve) calls it only if a rung needs it), scrubbed
of anything credential-shaped.

* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)

### s3dol.connection.normalize_credentials(value)

Normalise every accepted credential shape; reject the rest, each with
its own message (ADR-0012 D5). The only door is `S3Connection.__post_init__`.

```pycon
>>> normalize_credentials(None) is None
True
>>> normalize_credentials('prod')
ProfileCredentials(profile='prod')
>>> normalize_credentials(('AKIAXX', 'sec'))
StaticCredentials(access_key='AKIA'…, secret_key=***)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`CredentialProvider`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.CredentialProvider)]

### s3dol.connection.resolve(spec, environ, aws_config=None)

Pure resolution: no `os.environ`, no disk, no network (ADR-0012 D2).

`environ` is a plain mapping (pass `os.environ` at real call sites,
a dict in tests). `aws_config` is a pre-loaded, credential-scrubbed
config mapping, or a thunk for one ([`load_aws_config()`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.load_aws_config)) — called only
if a rung needs it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Resolution`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.Resolution)


# _autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md

# s3dol.errors

The s3dol error taxonomy and the single error-translation seam.

Design record: `misc/docs/decisions/0004-error-taxonomy.md` (the taxonomy, the
`(operation, code, status)` classification, the 403 policy, `ObjectArchived`)
and `misc/docs/decisions/0012-credential-and-endpoint-resolution.md` (the
`ConfigurationError` tree and the `S3DolWarning` tree).

Three rules govern this module:

1. **One seam.** [`translate_s3_errors()`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.translate_s3_errors) is the only place in the package
   that catches botocore exceptions. Everything else propagates.
2. \*\*Auth, config and transport errors are never translated to `KeyError`.\*\*
   A missing permission must not look like a missing key.
3. \*\*Classification keys on `(operation, code, status)`, never on exception
   type.\*\* HEAD responses have no body, so botocore’s modelled exceptions
   (`client.exceptions.NoSuchKey` …) never fire for them.

Everything classification-related here is pure: [`classify_client_error()`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.classify_client_error)
takes plain values (or a synthesized `ClientError`) and touches no network,
so the bulk of error tests are tier-1 unit tests — including body-less HEAD
errors, which moto cannot produce.

```pycon
>>> classify_client_error('GetObject', 'NoSuchKey', 404).kind
'object_absent'
>>> classify_client_error('HeadObject', '404', 404).kind  # HEAD is ambiguous
'ambiguous_head'
>>> classify_client_error('GetObject', 'AccessDenied', 403).kind
'access_denied'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`KINDS`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.KINDS)         | Kinds a classified error can be.                                           |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Rule`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.Rule)          | `((operation, code, status), kind)`.                                       |
| [`DEFAULT_RULES`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.DEFAULT_RULES) | The default classification table (ADR-0004 §2, measured against botocore). |

### Functions

| [`classify_client_error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.classify_client_error)(operation, code, status, \*)   | Classify a backend error by `(operation, code, status)`.                                                                                                                                                       |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`code_of`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.code_of)(client_error)                                | The `Error.Code` of a botocore `ClientError` (or `None`).                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`redact`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.redact)(text)                                         | Redact signed-URL query secrets from `text`.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`redact_url`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.redact_url)(url)                                      | A URL safe to display: userinfo, query and fragment removed.                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`status_of`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.status_of)(client_error)                              | The HTTP status of a botocore `ClientError` (or `None`).                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`translate_client_error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.translate_client_error)(error, \*, operation)         | Translate a botocore `ClientError` into the s3dol taxonomy.                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`translate_s3_errors`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.translate_s3_errors)(\*, operation[, key_arg])        | The one seam: decorate a Layer B method so botocore's `ClientError` becomes the s3dol taxonomy (ADR-0004 §1).                                                                                                  |
| [`translating_s3_errors`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.translating_s3_errors)(store, \*, operation[, key])   | Generator/inline form of the seam, for code the decorator cannot wrap (`__iter__` bodies: a decorated generator function returns its generator before the body runs, so the decorator's `except` never fires). |

### Classes

| [`Classified`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.Classified)(kind[, exception_type])   | The result of classifying a backend error.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`AccessDenied`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.AccessDenied)                                       | Permission denied.                                                                                                                    |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`AmbiguousResolution`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.AmbiguousResolution)                                | Resolution is legal but ambiguous (e.g. a named preset whose endpoint, supplied from the environment, matches no known host pattern). |
| [`AnonymousFallback`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.AnonymousFallback)                                  | Anonymous access was used as a fallback (reserved for a future `anon='auto'` — ADR-0012 D5 defers that feature to v1.x).              |
| [`BucketNotEmpty`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.BucketNotEmpty)                                     | Refusal to delete a non-empty bucket.                                                                                                 |
| [`BucketNotFound`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.BucketNotFound)                                     | The bucket is absent.                                                                                                                 |
| [`ConfigurationError`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError)                                 | A construction- or resolution-time misconfiguration (ADR-0012 D1).                                                                    |
| [`CredentialsError`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.CredentialsError)                                   | Credentials are missing, expired, or invalid.                                                                                         |
| [`InvalidEndpoint`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.InvalidEndpoint)                                    | An endpoint URL failed hygiene checks (userinfo/query/fragment — ADR-0012 D4: a URL is the residual credential carrier).              |
| [`KeyNotValid`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.KeyNotValid)                                        | The key is syntactically invalid (checked before the wire).                                                                           |
| [`MissingEndpoint`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.MissingEndpoint)                                    | The named preset needs an endpoint (or endpoint parameters) that nothing supplied (ADR-0012 C1).                                      |
| [`MissingPresetParam`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.MissingPresetParam)                                 | A preset's endpoint template has an unbound required parameter, so the row contributes no endpoint rung (ADR-0012 C1).                |
| [`NotSupported`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.NotSupported)                                       | The operation is not supported by this provider (names both).                                                                         |
| [`ObjectArchived`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ObjectArchived)(message, \*[, storage_class, ...])  | The object exists but is archived (e.g. Glacier) and cannot be read now.                                                              |
| [`ObjectNotFound`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ObjectNotFound)                                     | The object is absent.                                                                                                                 |
| [`PresetConflict`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.PresetConflict)                                     | An explicit argument contradicts a *pinned* (verified) preset value.                                                                  |
| [`PresetHostMismatch`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.PresetHostMismatch)                                 | The resolved endpoint's host matches a *different* provider's patterns than the preset you named (ADR-0012 C2).                       |

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error)

Permission denied. **Not** a `KeyError` — a missing permission must
not look like a missing key (ADR-0004 §1/§3).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.AmbiguousResolution

Bases: [`S3DolWarning`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3DolWarning)

### *exception* s3dol.errors.AnonymousFallback

Bases: [`S3DolWarning`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3DolWarning)

`anon='auto'` — ADR-0012 D5 defers that feature to v1.x).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.BucketNotEmpty

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error)

Refusal to delete a non-empty bucket. Use
`s3dol.delete_bucket(endpoint, name, force=True)` for the explicit
cascading form (ADR-0010 §3).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.BucketNotFound

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error), `_InformativeKeyError`

The bucket is absent.

Still a `KeyError`: for an object operation it is a key-space problem for
the caller; for a bucket operation it is the key of the endpoint mapping.

### *exception* s3dol.errors.InvalidEndpoint

Bases: [`ConfigurationError`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError)

An endpoint URL failed hygiene checks (userinfo/query/fragment —
ADR-0012 D4: a URL is the residual credential carrier).

### s3dol.errors.KINDS *= ('object_absent', 'bucket_absent', 'ambiguous_head', 'access_denied', 'credentials', 'invalid_key', 'archived', 'not_supported', 'wrong_region', 'delete_marker', 'transient', 'unknown')*

Kinds a classified error can be. Layer B maps kinds to behaviour; in
particular `ambiguous_head` triggers the one-`HeadBucket`
disambiguation of ADR-0004 §2 (HEAD has no body, so a missing key and a
missing bucket are both `('404', 404)` on real AWS).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.KeyNotValid

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error), `_InformativeKeyError`, [`ValueError`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError)

The key is syntactically invalid (checked before the wire).

Inherits from both `KeyError` and `ValueError` deliberately, so either
`except` works. Named `KeyNotValid` (not `KeyValidationError`) because
dol already ships two *different* classes called `KeyValidationError`
(ADR-0004 §5).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.MissingEndpoint

Bases: [`ConfigurationError`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError)

The named preset needs an endpoint (or endpoint parameters) that nothing
supplied (ADR-0012 C1).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.MissingPresetParam

Bases: [`MissingEndpoint`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.MissingEndpoint)

A preset’s endpoint template has an unbound required parameter, so the
row contributes no endpoint rung (ADR-0012 C1). A `MissingEndpoint`, so
either `except` works.

### *exception* s3dol.errors.NotSupported

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error)

The operation is not supported by this provider (names both).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.ObjectArchived(message, , storage_class=None, restore_status=None, restore=None)

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error), `_InformativeKeyError`

The object exists but is archived (e.g. Glacier) and cannot be read now.

A `KeyError`, deliberately and arguably (ADR-0004 §4): `k in store`
stays `True`, but `store[k]` fails as a `KeyError` so that
`store.get(k, default)` degrades to the not-available branch. Note that
only the *defaulted accessors* degrade — `dict(store)`, `.items()` and
`Mapping.__eq__` still raise. `setdefault`/`pop` are overridden in the
store to re-raise this instead of silently overwriting the archived object.

#### restore(days=1, , tier='Standard')

Request restoration of the archived object (if a handle was bound).

### *exception* s3dol.errors.ObjectNotFound

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error), `_InformativeKeyError`

The object is absent. The Mapping contract’s `KeyError`.

Bases: [`ConfigurationError`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError)

An explicit argument contradicts a *pinned* (verified) preset value.

than the preset you named (ADR-0012 C2).

First match wins; more specific rows come first.

### *exception* s3dol.errors.S3DolWarning

Bases: [`UserWarning`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#UserWarning)

### *exception* s3dol.errors.S3Error

Bases: [`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#Exception)

Base of every s3dol exception — `except S3Error` catches the package.

### *exception* s3dol.errors.S3PartialFailure(message, , succeeded, failures)

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error)

A bulk operation partially failed (ADR-0010 §2).

Not an `ExceptionGroup` — the package supports Python 3.10.

#### succeeded

keys the backend reported as deleted (absent keys are
reported as deleted too — S3’s semantics, documented, not hidden).

#### failures

mapping of key -> the error for that key.

### *exception* s3dol.errors.UnknownPresetParam

Bases: [`ConfigurationError`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError)

A parameter was bound that the preset’s templates do not use.

### s3dol.errors.classify_client_error(operation, code, status, , overrides=())

Classify a backend error by `(operation, code, status)`.

`overrides` rows (typically from a preset) are consulted first, so a
provider divergence is a table row, never a code branch.

```pycon
>>> classify_client_error('HeadBucket', None, 400,
...     overrides=((('HeadBucket', None, 400), 'bucket_absent'),)).kind
'bucket_absent'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Classified`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.Classified)

### s3dol.errors.code_of(client_error)

The `Error.Code` of a botocore `ClientError` (or `None`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### s3dol.errors.redact(text)

Redact signed-URL query secrets from `text`.

Error messages may name the operation, bucket, key, endpoint and code, but
never a credential, token, or signed URL — redaction is a tested function,
not a convention (ADR-0004 §7).

```pycon
>>> redact('https://b.s3.amazonaws.com/k?X-Amz-Signature=abc123&x=1')
'https://b.s3.amazonaws.com/k?X-Amz-Signature=REDACTED&x=1'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### s3dol.errors.redact_url(url)

A URL safe to display: userinfo, query and fragment removed.

A URL is the residual credential carrier (ADR-0012 D4). Endpoint hygiene
refuses those shapes for values *s3dol* is given, but an endpoint read
from `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` or an aws-config profile is not ours to
refuse — it must merely never be echoed intact.

```pycon
>>> redact_url('https://user:pw@minio.internal:9000/x?sig=abc#f')
'https://REDACTED@minio.internal:9000/x?<redacted>'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### s3dol.errors.status_of(client_error)

The HTTP status of a botocore `ClientError` (or `None`).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### s3dol.errors.translate_client_error(error, , operation, bucket=None, key=None, endpoint=None, overrides=(), deny_means_absent=False, head_ambiguity_resolver=None)

Translate a botocore `ClientError` into the s3dol taxonomy.

Returns the replacement exception, or `None` meaning \*propagate the
original\* (transient/unknown — rule 2 of the module docstring).

`head_ambiguity_resolver` resolves the body-less `HeadObject` 404
(ADR-0004 §2): it returns `True` iff the bucket is known reachable, in
which case the miss really is the object’s. It is only called for the
ambiguous case, so the common path costs nothing.

`deny_means_absent=True` classifies an object-op 403 as
`ObjectNotFound` — for deployments knowingly running the canonical
least-privilege policy that omits `s3:ListBucket` (ADR-0004 §3).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error)]

### s3dol.errors.translate_s3_errors(, operation, key_arg=None, \*\*translate_kwargs)

The one seam: decorate a Layer B method so botocore’s `ClientError`
becomes the s3dol taxonomy (ADR-0004 §1).

`key_arg` names the decorated function’s key *parameter* (resolved via
the call’s kwargs/positionals — never an attribute, so the key is not lost
the way azuredol’s `key_arg='blob'` loses it). The store instance is
expected to provide `_error_context()` returning
`dict(bucket=..., endpoint=..., overrides=..., deny_means_absent=...,
head_ambiguity_resolver=...)` — Layer B owns that context.

### s3dol.errors.translating_s3_errors(store, , operation, key=None, \*\*translate_kwargs)

Generator/inline form of the seam, for code the decorator cannot wrap
(`__iter__` bodies: a decorated generator function returns its generator
before the body runs, so the decorator’s `except` never fires).

Same contract as [`translate_s3_errors()`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.translate_s3_errors); the store supplies
`_error_context()`.


# _autosummary/s3dol.html.md

# s3dol

s3dol — S3 and S3-compatible object storage behind a dict-like interface.

The one-liner:

```default
import s3dol
s = s3dol.s3_store('my-bucket')          # MutableMapping[str, bytes]
s['k'] = b'v'; s['k']; list(s); del s['k']
```

Keyed capabilities are **sibling stores you index** (never methods — a dol key
wrapper would hand a method the unmapped key; ADR-0011):

```default
s3dol.handles(s)['k']    # ObjectHandle (ranged reads, streams, metadata)
s3dol.urls(s)['k']       # presigned URL
s3dol.info(s)['k']       # ObjectInfo (one HeadObject)
s3dol.listed_info(s)['k']  # ObjectInfo from one LIST (a snapshot)
```

Non-keyed operations are free functions taking the store first:

```default
s3dol.sub(s, 'folder/')          s3dol.prefixes(s)
s3dol.delete_many(s, keys)       s3dol.delete_bucket(endpoint, name, force=True)
```

Test without a cloud: `from s3dol.testing import mock_s3, run_conformance`.
Migrating from v0? `s3dol.diagnose(**your_S3Store_kwargs)` prints what
resolves, from where, and whether v1 moves it. The legacy `S3Store` keeps
working via `s3dol.store` (deprecated, removed in v2).

Everything here loads lazily (PEP 562): `import s3dol` does not import boto3.

### *class* s3dol.BucketListedInfo(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

`k -> ObjectInfo` from the listing rows, not one `HeadObject` per key.

The first access (a lookup or an iteration) pages through `ListObjectsV2`
once and keeps `{key: ObjectInfo}` (`size`, `last_modified`, `etag`,
`storage_class`; `content_type` and the other HEAD-only fields stay
`None`). It is **lazy and a snapshot**: later writes are not seen; make a
new `listed_info(store)` to refresh. A whole-bucket ETag comparison costs
one LIST per 1000 keys.

### *class* s3dol.BucketReader(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketCollection`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketCollection), `KvReader`

+ `__getitem__` -> bytes (or the read strategy’s value type).

#### url_for(k, , expires_in=3600, client_method='get_object', \*\*params)

Presigned URL for `k` — **the one keyed method** (ADR-0011 D3b),
kept solely because `dol.SupportsUrlFor` requires a *method* and
`dol.content_url` reaches it by `getattr`. The canonical form is
`s3dol.urls(store)[k]`.

Guarded to be correct-or-loud, never silently wrong:

- **unwrapped store**: `k` is a key in this store’s own key space,
  so the URL addresses `self._id_of_key(k)`. Correct, and this is
  also the contract `dol.content_url` calls under — it resolves the
  key through the *outer* layers and stops at the layer owning
  `url_for`, “because that layer applies its own”
  (`dol/content.py`);
- **this leaf has ever been wrapped**: **raises**. Two call paths then
  reach this one signature with *different key domains* and nothing
  distinguishes them: `dol.content_url` hands over a key already
  mapped through the wrapper layers, while a direct
  `wrapped.url_for(k)` (delegation) hands over the raw outer key.
  Applying `_id_of_key` is right for the first and wrong for the
  second; re-resolving through the chain is right for the second and
  double-transforms the first. Since a wrong presigned URL addresses a
  *different real object*, the only honest answer is refusal, naming
  the sibling store — which is correct by construction because it goes
  through `__getitem__` (ADR-0011 D2/D3b, and see the note below);
- **anonymous connection**: returns `None` (`SupportsUrlFor` is
  `Optional[str]`; raising would turn a public-bucket streaming
  fallback into a 500 — ADR-0012 D5). The check reads the built
  client’s signature version, never `spec.anon`.

#### NOTE
This refusal is a *finding*, not a limitation we chose.
ADR-0011 D3b expected a guarded method to serve both paths; it
cannot, on a leaf that owns its prefix. Reported upstream on
dol#86/#83 as evidence that a keyed capability *method* is
unfixable in the general case, and that the sibling-store form is
the only one correct by construction.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### *class* s3dol.BucketStore(bucket, , connection=None, prefix='', delimiter='/', reads=None, writes=None, on_missing_bucket='assume', strict_delete=False)

Bases: [`BucketReader`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketReader), `KvPersister`

+ `__setitem__` / `__delitem__`. The user-facing read-write store.

#### pop(k) → v, remove specified key and return the corresponding value.

If key is not found, d is returned if given, otherwise KeyError is raised.

#### setdefault(k) → D.get(k,d), also set D[k]=d if k not in D

#### update(other=(), , \*\*kwargs)

If E present and has a .keys() method, does:     for k in E.keys(): D[k] = E[k]
If E present and lacks .keys() method, does:     for (k, v) in E: D[k] = v
In either case, this is followed by: for k, v in F.items(): D[k] = v

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### *class* s3dol.BucketUrls(\*args, expires_in=3600, client_method='get_object', \*\*kwargs)

### *class* s3dol.CallableCredentials(fetch)

Bases: [`CredentialProvider`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.CredentialProvider)

A picklable zero-arg callable returning a mapping with keys
`access_key`/`secret_key` (aliases: `key`/`secret`), optional
`token`, optional `expires_at`/`expiry_time` (ISO 8601). With an
expiry, credentials are refreshable — the callable is re-invoked by

#### provenance()

* **Return type:**

### *class* s3dol.Capabilities(list_objects_v2=True, batch_delete=True, presigned_post=True, multipart=True, max_multipart_parts=10000, min_part_size=5242880, object_tagging=True, versioning=True, conditional_writes=True, consistency='strong')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a backend supports. A *static declared table*, never a probe
(a probe costs a round-trip, is wrong under partial permissions, and can’t
be trusted anyway — ADR-0003 §2). Missing capabilities are handled
per-capability: emulate when exact (batch delete -> loop), substitute when
equivalent (ListObjectsV2 -> V1), raise `NotSupported` when there is no
honest fallback. Never silently degrade correctness.

### *class* s3dol.Chunks(chunks, consumed=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The value is the concatenation of an iterable of `bytes` chunks.
**One-shot** unless the iterable is re-iterable (a list is; a generator is
not — and a consumed generator writes `b''`, which is why assigning the
same one-shot ref twice is a documented error).

### *class* s3dol.DailyByteBudget(limit_bytes, \*, ledger=None, today=<function DailyByteBudget.<lambda>>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A per-day byte budget (one instance per tenant); call it to reserve.

`ledger` is any `MutableMapping[str, int]` (default: in-memory) keyed
by day, so persistence is a one-argument swap (a `dol` store, a file…).
`today` is the clock seam. Reservation is optimistic (the *maximum* the
form allows), and a form holds exactly one key, so re-posting cannot multiply the budget.

### *exception* s3dol.ObjectArchived(message, , storage_class=None, restore_status=None, restore=None)

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error), `_InformativeKeyError`

The object exists but is archived (e.g. Glacier) and cannot be read now.

A `KeyError`, deliberately and arguably (ADR-0004 §4): `k in store`
stays `True`, but `store[k]` fails as a `KeyError` so that
`store.get(k, default)` degrades to the not-available branch. Note that
only the *defaulted accessors* degrade — `dict(store)`, `.items()` and
`Mapping.__eq__` still raise. `setdefault`/`pop` are overridden in the
store to re-raise this instead of silently overwriting the archived object.

#### restore(days=1, , tier='Standard')

Request restoration of the archived object (if a handle was bound).

### *class* s3dol.ObjectHandle(bucket, key, , connection=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One object, key bound **at construction** — which is what makes it
immune to the delegation trap (a key codec over the store cannot corrupt a
key that was resolved before the handle existed; ADR-0011 D1, following
`azuredol.BlobHandle`). This is where ranged reads, streaming,
download-to-disk, metadata and presigned URLs live.

Download to disk (never fully in memory). Accepts a path or

### *class* s3dol.Preset(name, addressing_style, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, checksum=None, payload_signing_enabled=None, capabilities=Capabilities(list_objects_v2=True, batch_delete=True, presigned_post=True, multipart=True, max_multipart_parts=10000, min_part_size=5242880, object_tagging=True, versioning=True, conditional_writes=True, consistency='strong'), presign_endpoint_url=None, presign_addressing_style=None, params=(), host_patterns=(), requires_endpoint=False, soft=False, config_kwargs=(), error_overrides=(), verified=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One provider’s facts. Public, shareable, committable config — which is
why there is **no credential slot**, structurally (ADR-0012 D4).

`endpoint_url`/`region_name` may contain `{placeholders}`; bind them
with [`bind()`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.Preset.bind). A row whose endpoint template has an unbound *required*
placeholder contributes no endpoint rung (ADR-0012 C1).

#### addressing_style *: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['path', 'virtual']*

Mandatory; no default; `'auto'` is illegal (ADR-0012 D4).

#### bind(\*\*params)

A copy of this row with template `params` bound.

```pycon
>>> r2 = get_preset('r2').bind(account_id='abc123')
>>> r2.bound_endpoint()
'https://abc123.r2.cloudflarestorage.com'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Preset`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.Preset)

#### bound_endpoint(, region_name=None)

The endpoint URL with params bound, or `None` if the template has
unbound placeholders (C1: an unbound row contributes no rung —
`preset='minio'` silently becoming AWS is structurally impossible).

`region_name` binds a `{region_name}` placeholder, per the region
ladder’s first rung (ADR-0012 D3).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### *class* s3dol.S3Connection(preset=None, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, profile=None, credentials=None, anon=False, signature_version='s3v4', addressing_style=None, checksum=None, payload_signing_enabled=None, verify=None, client_kwargs=(), deny_means_absent=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A frozen, picklable connection spec. No live objects — ever.

Construction performs no I/O and does not import boto3 (ADR-0002); the
client is built lazily, once, under a per-instance lock (CPython ≥3.12
removed `cached_property`’s lock deliberately — measured: 8 racing
threads → 8 clients without one).

`__post_init__` is the only door: every normalisation and contradiction
check happens here, so a bad shape dies at construction with a message,
not later inside botocore.

```pycon
>>> S3Connection(anon=True, profile='prod')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
s3dol.errors.ConfigurationError: ...
```

#### *property* client

The boto3 S3 client — built lazily, once, under the lock.

#### *property* presign_client

The client presigned URLs are generated with.

For most providers this is [`client`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.S3Connection.client). Two providers genuinely
need different config for presigning than for the API (ADR-0003 §1):
Hetzner presigns virtual-hosted while the API is path-style; R2
presigns only on the S3 API domain. When the resolved preset carries
`presign_endpoint_url`/`presign_addressing_style`, a second client
is built (lazily, once, under the same lock) from the merged config.

#### resolution(environ=None, aws_config=<function load_aws_config>)

Resolve against the real environment by default (a thin impure
wrapper over the pure [`resolve()`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.resolve)).

* **Return type:**
  [`Resolution`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.Resolution)

### s3dol.S3Store(bucket_name, , make_bucket=None, path=None, aws_access_key_id=None, aws_secret_access_key=None, aws_session_token=None, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, profile_name=None, skip_bucket_check=None, is_supabase_endpoint=None)

DEPRECATED — the v0 entry point, kept working until v2.

Use [`s3dol.s3_store()`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.s3_store) instead: `s3_store(bucket, prefix=...)`.

fixes only (explicit endpoint/credentials honoured; listing errors raise
instead of returning `[]`; writes no longer create buckets unless asked)
and announce themselves via `S3DolResolutionChanged` when they change

### s3dol.delete_bucket(endpoint, name, , force=False)

Delete bucket `name`. Refuses a non-empty bucket unless
`force=True`, in which case the cascade **paginates** — v0 listed one
page, deleted ≤1000 objects, then failed: a partial, non-idempotent
destruction (ADR-0010 §3). A free function, not a method (ADR-0011 D4).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### s3dol.delete_many(store, keys)

Bulk delete (ADR-0010 §2; a free function per ADR-0011 D4 — keyed +
destructive + delegated is the census’s data-destroying shape).

Chunks at 1000 (AWS’s cap), parses the `Errors` list out of the HTTP
200 response, and on partial failure raises one [`S3PartialFailure`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.S3PartialFailure)
carrying `.succeeded` and `.failures`. Absent keys are reported by S3
as `Deleted` — this function does **not** distinguish them (same
idempotency as `del store[k]`).

Keys are the *caller’s* keys: with the store held as an argument the
chain is resolved via `dol.inner_most_key` (alive store — no weakref
hole). Validate-the-target caveat (D4): the first argument must be an
s3dol store or a dol wrapper over one.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### s3dol.diagnose(connection=None, , environ=None, aws_config=None, file=None, \*\*kwargs)

Print (and return) the resolution report. Never raises.

Call it either with a ready [`S3Connection`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.S3Connection), with
`S3Connection` kwargs, or — the migration case — with exactly the kwargs
you pass `s3dol.store.S3Store` today (`bucket_name=`, `path=`,
`profile_name=`, …), which additionally prints the v0-vs-v1
divergence table.

```pycon
>>> report = diagnose(endpoint_url='http://localhost:9000',
...                   environ={}, file=io.StringIO())
>>> 'endpoint_url' in report and 'resolution' in report.lower()
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### s3dol.handles(store)

The sibling store of [`ObjectHandle`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.ObjectHandle)s: `handles(s)[k]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketHandles`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketHandles)

### s3dol.info(store)

The sibling store of [`ObjectInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.ObjectInfo): `info(s)[k]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketInfo)

### s3dol.listed_info(store)

The sibling store of [`ObjectInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.ObjectInfo) built from one paginated LIST:
`listed_info(s)[k]` (a lazy snapshot; see [`BucketListedInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.BucketListedInfo)).

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketListedInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketListedInfo)

### s3dol.prefixes(store)

The ‘directories’ one level under the store’s scope, \*\*relative to the
caller’s key space\*\* — one `ListObjectsV2(Delimiter='/')` reading
`CommonPrefixes` (which v0 parsed and then called from nowhere;
ADR-0009). Through a dol wrapper chain, the listing is rooted at the
caller’s scope (each prefix layer’s contribution) and results are mapped
back **outward** (`_key_of_id` per layer, innermost first — the inverse
walk `dol` does not provide; ADR-0011 D3). A wrapper whose codec cannot
express the scope raises — loud, not wrong.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

### s3dol.presigned_upload(store, , key_prefix, max_bytes, content_type, min_bytes=0, expires_in=900, budget=None)

A presigned POST form for ONE new object under `key_prefix`.

`content_type` is required: pass the one type to accept, or `None` to
explicitly accept any (then a holder can store `text/html`: do not serve
such objects from a trusted origin).

`key_prefix` must end with the store’s delimiter (`tenant-7/` cannot
match `tenant-77/`) and is in the *store’s* key space (the store’s own
prefix is prepended, like every other s3dol key). The object key is
server-generated (`PresignedUpload.key`). Returns `None` for an
anonymous store (no signing capability, as [`s3dol.urls()`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.urls) does).

Raises [`ConfigurationError`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.ConfigurationError) for a bad prefix, size range or
`expires_in`, and [`UploadBudgetExceeded`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.UploadBudgetExceeded) if `budget` refuses.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`PresignedUpload`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.PresignedUpload)]

### s3dol.register_preset(preset, , overwrite=False)

Add a row. Open-closed: adding a provider is adding a row.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### s3dol.resolve(spec, environ, aws_config=None)

Pure resolution: no `os.environ`, no disk, no network (ADR-0012 D2).

`environ` is a plain mapping (pass `os.environ` at real call sites,
a dict in tests). `aws_config` is a pre-loaded, credential-scrubbed
config mapping, or a thunk for one (`load_aws_config()`) — called only
if a rung needs it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Resolution`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.Resolution)

### s3dol.s3_store(bucket, , prefix='', preset=None, connection=None, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, profile=None, credentials=None, anon=False, on_missing_bucket='assume', readonly=False, value_codec=None, reads=None, writes=None)

One bucket as a `MutableMapping[str, bytes]` (a `Mapping` when
`readonly=True`).

Annotated (deliberately) as the abstract Mapping, **not** `-> BucketStore`:
with `value_codec` the concrete type is a generated `dol` wrapper class
that is *not* a `BucketStore` subclass. (v0 annotated its factory
`-> Store` and returned something that was not one; inverting that lie
is not an improvement — architecture.md.)

Connection axes (`preset`/`endpoint_url`/`region_name`/`profile`/
`credentials`/`anon`) are conveniences that build an
[`S3Connection`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.S3Connection); pass `connection=` instead for
full control (they are mutually exclusive with it).

### s3dol.sub(store, prefix)

A store scoped to `prefix`, **in the caller’s key space** (D3).

Two branches, deliberately different (each documented in the ADR):

- **unwrapped s3dol store**: `leaf._with(prefix=...)` — cheap, keeps
  server-side prefix pushdown, returns the same class;
- **dol-wrapped store**: composes `Pipe(filt_iter.prefixes(p),
  KeyCodecs.prefixed(p))` over the *outer* store (filter FIRST — the only
  safe composition, ADR-0006 §1), which preserves the user’s codecs but
  loses pushdown (a full scan filtered client-side; D8 closed this: the
  cheap path is the unwrapped branch) and returns a different type.

### s3dol.urls(store, , expires_in=3600, client_method='get_object')

The sibling store of presigned URLs: `urls(s)[k]`.

* **Return type:**
  [`BucketUrls`](_autosummary/s3dol.capabilities.html.md#s3dol.capabilities.BucketUrls)

# _autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md

# s3dol.presets

Provider presets: config rows, not subclasses.

Design record: `misc/docs/decisions/0003-provider-presets-and-capabilities.md`
(the survey of 16 backends, the checksum analysis, capabilities policy) amended
by `misc/docs/decisions/0012-credential-and-endpoint-resolution.md` §D4
(`params`/`host_patterns`/`requires_endpoint`/`soft`/`config_kwargs`,
derived `pinned`; `signature_version` and `client_kwargs` moved to the
connection; `addressing_style` mandatory with `'auto'` illegal; the
structural no-credential rule).

A provider divergence is a row in this registry — never a subclass, never an
endpoint-substring branch in the hot path. Users register their own rows:

```pycon
>>> row = Preset(name='mycorp', addressing_style='path',
...              endpoint_url='https://s3.mycorp.example', requires_endpoint=False)
>>> register(row)
>>> get_preset('mycorp').endpoint_url
'https://s3.mycorp.example'
>>> unregister('mycorp')  # (cleanup for this doctest)
```

Most builtin rows are **doc-sourced, not verified against a live endpoint** —
they say so via `verified=False`. Wrong values mostly fail loudly, which is
the acceptable failure mode; `pinned` (which makes a row’s region literal
conflict-raising) is derived and *gated on* `verified`, so it is dormant
until a row earns evidence (ADR-0012 D4).

### Module Attributes

| [`CONFIG_KWARGS_ALLOWLIST`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.CONFIG_KWARGS_ALLOWLIST)   | `Config`-constructor kwargs a preset row may carry.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| `available_presets`()                                                                       |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`detect_preset`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.detect_preset)(endpoint_url)                | Detection (resolution pass 2): the non-soft row whose `host_patterns` match the resolved endpoint's host.                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`get_preset`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.get_preset)(name)                           | Look a row up by name; unknown names raise, naming the registry.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`register`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.register)(preset, \*[, overwrite])          | Add a row.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`unregister`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.unregister)(name)                           | Remove a row (mostly for tests).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`validate_endpoint_hygiene`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.validate_endpoint_hygiene)(url, \*[, what]) | Refuse credential-carrying URL shapes: userinfo in the netloc, a query string, or a fragment (ADR-0012 D4 — a query-string endpoint is accepted by botocore and retained verbatim in `client.meta.endpoint_url`, so it would leak into `diagnose()` and tracebacks). |

### Classes

| [`Capabilities`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.Capabilities)([list_objects_v2, ...])   | What a backend supports.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| [`Preset`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.Preset)(name, addressing_style[, ...])  | One provider's facts.      |

### s3dol.presets.CONFIG_KWARGS_ALLOWLIST *= frozenset({'connect_timeout', 'max_pool_connections', 'read_timeout', 'tcp_keepalive'})*

`Config`-constructor kwargs a preset row may carry. Scalars only, and
`proxies`/`proxies_config`/`client_context_params` are structurally
excluded — a preset must not be able to smuggle a credential-bearing proxy
URL (ADR-0012 D4).

### *class* s3dol.presets.Capabilities(list_objects_v2=True, batch_delete=True, presigned_post=True, multipart=True, max_multipart_parts=10000, min_part_size=5242880, object_tagging=True, versioning=True, conditional_writes=True, consistency='strong')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a backend supports. A *static declared table*, never a probe
(a probe costs a round-trip, is wrong under partial permissions, and can’t
be trusted anyway — ADR-0003 §2). Missing capabilities are handled
per-capability: emulate when exact (batch delete -> loop), substitute when
equivalent (ListObjectsV2 -> V1), raise `NotSupported` when there is no
honest fallback. Never silently degrade correctness.

### *class* s3dol.presets.Preset(name, addressing_style, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, checksum=None, payload_signing_enabled=None, capabilities=Capabilities(list_objects_v2=True, batch_delete=True, presigned_post=True, multipart=True, max_multipart_parts=10000, min_part_size=5242880, object_tagging=True, versioning=True, conditional_writes=True, consistency='strong'), presign_endpoint_url=None, presign_addressing_style=None, params=(), host_patterns=(), requires_endpoint=False, soft=False, config_kwargs=(), error_overrides=(), verified=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One provider’s facts. Public, shareable, committable config — which is
why there is **no credential slot**, structurally (ADR-0012 D4).

`endpoint_url`/`region_name` may contain `{placeholders}`; bind them
with [`bind()`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.Preset.bind). A row whose endpoint template has an unbound *required*
placeholder contributes no endpoint rung (ADR-0012 C1).

#### addressing_style *: [Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['path', 'virtual']*

Mandatory; no default; `'auto'` is illegal (ADR-0012 D4).

#### bind(\*\*params)

A copy of this row with template `params` bound.

```pycon
>>> r2 = get_preset('r2').bind(account_id='abc123')
>>> r2.bound_endpoint()
'https://abc123.r2.cloudflarestorage.com'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Preset`](_autosummary/s3dol.presets.html.md#s3dol.presets.Preset)

#### bound_endpoint(, region_name=None)

The endpoint URL with params bound, or `None` if the template has
unbound placeholders (C1: an unbound row contributes no rung —
`preset='minio'` silently becoming AWS is structurally impossible).

`region_name` binds a `{region_name}` placeholder, per the region
ladder’s first rung (ADR-0012 D3).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### checksum *: [Optional](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[Literal](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Literal)['when_supported', 'when_required']]* *= None*

`None` == the row makes no claim (the ladder continues — ADR-0012 D3).

# _autosummary/s3dol.reads.html.md

# s3dol.reads

Read strategies (ADR-0005 §6): what `s[k]` returns.

`s[k]` returns `bytes` — always, under the default strategy, because the
N1 canonical form demands it. `stream_reads` is the documented *runtime*
variation (the store’s values become chunk iterators); it does not change the
class’s static value type — honest typing there would need a generic store,
which v1 does not do.

Ranged reads and download-to-disk are per-object concerns and live on
`ObjectHandle` (`handle.read(offset=, length=)`, `handle.download_to`),
not here — a store-level “ranged” strategy would need a per-key range, which a
Mapping cannot express.

Strategies are frozen dataclasses, not closures, because every s3dol store
must pickle (ADR-0008 §6) and a store carries its strategy.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE`](_autosummary/s3dol.reads.html.md#s3dol.reads.DEFAULT_CHUNK_SIZE)   | Default streaming chunk size (8 MiB, matching the write side).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| `bytes_reads`()            |    |
|----------------------------|----|
| `stream_reads`(\*\*kwargs) |    |

### Classes

| [`BytesReads`](_autosummary/s3dol.reads.html.md#s3dol.reads.BytesReads)()                     | The default: one `GetObject`, fully read -> `bytes`.                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ReadStrategy`](_autosummary/s3dol.reads.html.md#s3dol.reads.ReadStrategy)(\*args, \*\*kwargs) |                                                                                   |
| [`StreamReads`](_autosummary/s3dol.reads.html.md#s3dol.reads.StreamReads)([chunk_size])        | Values become lazy chunk iterators (the body streams; nothing is held in memory). |

### *class* s3dol.reads.BytesReads

The default: one `GetObject`, fully read -> `bytes`.

### *class* s3dol.reads.StreamReads(chunk_size=8388608)
