# _autosummary/s3dol.recipes.html.md

# s3dol.recipes

Layer C — the one-liner factory and codec facades. Composition ONLY.

If a recipe cannot be expressed as Layer B + `dol` wrappers, that is evidence
the capability belongs in Layer B as a *parameter* — this module never grows a
class statement (ADR-0001; the rule that keeps per-vendor classes from
reappearing).

The one-liner:

```default
s = s3dol.s3_store('my-bucket')                     # zero ceremony
s = s3dol.s3_store('my-bucket', prefix='logs/')     # scoped
s = s3dol.s3_store('pub-bucket', anon=True)         # public data
```

With `on_missing_bucket='assume'` (the default; no probe, ever — ADR-0010)
the two-line quickstart raises on a bucket that does not exist yet; start from
nothing with `on_missing_bucket='create'`.

### Functions

| [`s3_store`](_autosummary/s3dol.recipes.html.md#s3dol.recipes.s3_store)(bucket, \*[, prefix, preset, ...])   | One bucket as a `MutableMapping[str, bytes]` (a `Mapping` when `readonly=True`).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### s3dol.recipes.s3_store(bucket, , prefix='', preset=None, connection=None, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, profile=None, credentials=None, anon=False, on_missing_bucket='assume', readonly=False, value_codec=None, reads=None, writes=None)

One bucket as a `MutableMapping[str, bytes]` (a `Mapping` when
`readonly=True`).

Annotated (deliberately) as the abstract Mapping, **not** `-> BucketStore`:
with `value_codec` the concrete type is a generated `dol` wrapper class
that is *not* a `BucketStore` subclass. (v0 annotated its factory
`-> Store` and returned something that was not one; inverting that lie
is not an improvement — architecture.md.)

Connection axes (`preset`/`endpoint_url`/`region_name`/`profile`/
`credentials`/`anon`) are conveniences that build an
[`S3Connection`](_autosummary/s3dol.connection.html.md#s3dol.connection.S3Connection); pass `connection=` instead for
full control (they are mutually exclusive with it).


# _autosummary/s3dol.store.html.md

# s3dol.store

COMPAT SHIM — the v0 `S3Store`, forwarded onto the v1 machinery.

Removed in v2. This module **must survive as an importable module**: external
dependents do `from s3dol.store import S3Store` (fully qualified), not
`from s3dol import S3Store` (ADR-0007 §3).

The shim keeps v0’s exact signature (`bucket_name` positional-or-keyword,
`path=` not renamed, the `make_bucket` tri-state, and
`is_supabase_endpoint=` which an early draft forgot) and is \*\*a fix delivery
mechanism\*\*: callers get the corrected endpoint/credential resolution without
changing a line. Three v0 behaviours a dependent’s *passing tests* rely on are
deliberately preserved here (and only here — ADR-0007 §4):

- `store[k] = 'a str'` is accepted (encoded utf-8, with a
  `DeprecationWarning`);
- `store['folder/']` returns a sub-store;
- `del store[absent]` silently succeeds (v1 deletes are idempotent anyway).

And one v0 behaviour is preserved on the Supabase branch only: the read-side
de-chunker for objects that v0’s misconfigured writes stored with their
`aws-chunked` HTTP framing verbatim (ADR-0003 §3). It is implemented
*correctly* here (multi-chunk; full-parse-or-passthrough) where v0’s truncated
multi-chunk payloads. Per ADR-0003’s sequencing rule the codec is not deleted
until a repair path ships — [`detect_chunked_framing()`](_autosummary/s3dol.store.html.md#s3dol.store.detect_chunked_framing) is that path’s
diagnostic.

When v1 resolves a call differently than v0 *effectively* did (v0 dropped an
explicit `endpoint_url` whenever env credentials were set, and let env
credentials override explicit ones), the shim warns with
[`S3DolResolutionChanged`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3DolResolutionChanged) — the ADR-0012 D7 differential.
This module and that warning die together in v2.

### Functions

| [`S3Store`](_autosummary/s3dol.store.html.md#s3dol.store.S3Store)(bucket_name, \*[, make_bucket, path, ...])   | DEPRECATED — the v0 entry point, kept working until v2.                                                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dechunk_aws_chunked`](_autosummary/s3dol.store.html.md#s3dol.store.dechunk_aws_chunked)(data)                            | Undo verbatim-persisted `aws-chunked` framing, if present.                                                      |
| [`detect_chunked_framing`](_autosummary/s3dol.store.html.md#s3dol.store.detect_chunked_framing)(store, \*[, sample])          | Which of the first `sample` keys hold verbatim `aws-chunked` framing (objects corrupted by v0 Supabase writes). |

### s3dol.store.S3Store(bucket_name, , make_bucket=None, path=None, aws_access_key_id=None, aws_secret_access_key=None, aws_session_token=None, endpoint_url=None, region_name=None, profile_name=None, skip_bucket_check=None, is_supabase_endpoint=None)

DEPRECATED — the v0 entry point, kept working until v2.

Use [`s3dol.s3_store()`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.s3_store) instead: `s3_store(bucket, prefix=...)`.

Signature is v0’s exactly (`path=` not renamed; `make_bucket`
tri-state maps `True -> on_missing_bucket='create'`, `False ->
'raise'`, `None -> 'assume'`). Behaviour differences vs v0 are bug
fixes only (explicit endpoint/credentials honoured; listing errors raise
instead of returning `[]`; writes no longer create buckets unless asked)
and announce themselves via `S3DolResolutionChanged` when they change
this call’s resolution.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.MutableMapping)

### s3dol.store.dechunk_aws_chunked(data)

Undo verbatim-persisted `aws-chunked` framing, if present.

Full-parse-or-passthrough: either the ENTIRE payload parses as chunked
framing (every chunk header, every CRLF, through the terminal `0` chunk)
and the concatenated chunks are returned, or the payload is returned
untouched. v0’s parser truncated any payload larger than one chunk and
misfired on payloads that merely *started* with hex digits; requiring a
complete valid parse removes both failure modes (a random payload that
happens to be a complete chunked document is astronomically unlikely).

```pycon
>>> dechunk_aws_chunked(b'5\r\nhello\r\n0\r\n\r\n')
b'hello'
>>> framed = b'3\r\nabc\r\n2\r\nde\r\n0\r\nx-amz-checksum-crc32:AAAA\r\n\r\n'
>>> dechunk_aws_chunked(framed)  # multi-chunk (v0 truncated this)
b'abcde'
>>> dechunk_aws_chunked(b'cafe is hex-ish but not framed')
b'cafe is hex-ish but not framed'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### s3dol.store.detect_chunked_framing(store, , sample=20)

Which of the first `sample` keys hold verbatim `aws-chunked`
framing (objects corrupted by v0 Supabase writes). The repair path:
`store[k] = dechunk_aws_chunked(raw[k])` per flagged key, reading raw
bytes through an un-codec’d store.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)


# _autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md

# s3dol.testing

`s3dol.testing` — a shipped in-memory fake and the exported conformance
suite (ADR-0008). Downstream users can test services that take a store as a
dependency with **no network, no docker, no moto**:

```default
from s3dol.testing import mock_s3

def test_my_service():
    assert MediaService(mock_s3()).url('a')
```

The fake is not a re-implementation: [`FakeBucketStore`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeBucketStore) *is* the real
[`BucketStore`](_autosummary/s3dol.base.html.md#s3dol.base.BucketStore) with only the backend protocol (the `_op_*`
seam of ADR-0002) swapped for a dict — so the prefix arithmetic, key validity,
error taxonomy (the fake raises *synthesized botocore ClientErrors* through
the same translation seam), guards and Mapping semantics are structurally
identical, and drift fails the same conformance suite that gates the real
store.

The suite is parameterized by capability flags: `mock_s3()` runs the
structural presign assertion (2a) but not the fetch-it assertion (2b — there
is no HTTP server), so the honest claim is  *“the same suite, parameterized by
an \`\`endpoint_is_fetchable\`\` capability”* (ADR-0008).

### Functions

| [`mock_s3`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.mock_s3)([bucket, prefix, data, ...])   | An in-process fake `BucketStore`: no network, no docker, no moto.    |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`run_conformance`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.run_conformance)(make_store, \*[, ...]) | Assert the s3dol store laws against a fresh store from `make_store`. |

### Classes

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`FakeBucketInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeBucketInfo)(\*args[, backing])                  |                                                              |
| [`FakeBucketListedInfo`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeBucketListedInfo)(\*args[, backing])            |                                                              |
| [`FakeBucketStore`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeBucketStore)(\*args[, backing])                 | The real `BucketStore` over a dict backend.                  |
| [`FakeBucketUrls`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeBucketUrls)(\*args[, backing])                  |                                                              |
| [`FakeObjectHandle`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeObjectHandle)(bucket, key, \*, backing[, anon]) | The fake's per-object escape hatch (mirrors `ObjectHandle`). |

### s3dol.testing.mock_s3(bucket='mock-bucket', , prefix='', data=None, bucket_exists=True, anon=False)

An in-process fake `BucketStore`: no network, no docker, no moto.

`data` seeds the bucket with *absolute* (wire) keys -> bytes.

```pycon
>>> s = mock_s3(data={'logs/a.txt': b'hi', 'other/z': b'no'}, prefix='logs')
>>> list(s), s['a.txt']
(['a.txt'], b'hi')
>>> s['b'] = b'new'; sorted(s)

```

* **Return type:**
  [`FakeBucketStore`](_autosummary/s3dol.testing.html.md#s3dol.testing.FakeBucketStore)

### s3dol.testing.run_conformance(make_store, \*, endpoint_is_fetchable=False, normalize=<function <lambda>>, check_pickle=True, check_urls=True, secret=None)

Assert the s3dol store laws against a fresh store from `make_store`.

`make_store` must return an EMPTY, writable store (each call may return
a new one over the same empty backend). `normalize` is the per-layer
canonical form of ADR-0005 N3 (identity for Layer B; `json.loads ∘
json.dumps` for a json recipe, …). `secret`, when given, is asserted
absent from every repr this suite touches.

Sibling packages and user code are welcome to run this against their own
stores — that is why it ships in the package rather than in `tests/`.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)


# _autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md

# s3dol.uploads

Direct-to-S3 browser uploads: a presigned POST scoped to a key prefix.

A browser can upload straight to S3 without the server relaying bytes: the
server issues a presigned POST form whose signed policy pins

- the **exact key** (server-generated `<prefix><random token>`: the client
  never picks a filename, so it can neither overwrite a sibling object nor
  smuggle `..` segments; a form holds one object, and re-posting with it only
  overwrites that object, so the byte budget cannot be multiplied),
- a **content-length range** (`min_bytes`..\`\`max_bytes\`\`),
- the **content type** (optional), and
- an **expiry** (the 7-day SigV4 cap; an STS session’s own expiry still ends it sooner).

Before signing, an optional `budget` callable is asked to reserve the bytes
(`budget(max_bytes)` raises [`UploadBudgetExceeded`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.UploadBudgetExceeded) to refuse, and may return a `release()` callable that is called if signing fails), so a
daily per-tenant byte budget is enforced *before* any form exists.
[`DailyByteBudget`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.DailyByteBudget) is the ready-made one; any callable works.

The function is host-agnostic: it takes the store, the prefix and the limits
as arguments, and the web app mounts it behind its own auth:

```default
form = s3dol.presigned_upload(
    store, key_prefix='tenant-7/', max_bytes=5_000_000, content_type='image/png')
form.url, form.fields      # hand both to the browser's <form>/FormData
```

```pycon
>>> from s3dol.uploads import DailyByteBudget
>>> budget = DailyByteBudget(100, today=lambda: '2026-01-01')
>>> _ = budget(60); _ = budget(40)
>>> budget(1)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
s3dol.uploads.UploadBudgetExceeded: daily upload budget exceeded: 100 of 100 bytes already reserved, 1 requested
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXPIRES_IN`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXPIRES_IN)   | long enough to pick a file, short enough to not be a standing upload credential.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`presigned_upload`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.presigned_upload)(store, \*, key_prefix, ...)   | A presigned POST form for ONE new object under `key_prefix`.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`DailyByteBudget`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.DailyByteBudget)(limit_bytes, \*[, ledger, today])   | A per-day byte budget (one instance per tenant); call it to reserve.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`PresignedUpload`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.PresignedUpload)(url[, fields, key, ...])            | What the browser needs: POST `fields` + a `file` part to `url`.        |

### Exceptions

| [`UploadBudgetExceeded`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.UploadBudgetExceeded)   | The tenant's byte budget cannot cover this upload; no form was signed.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### s3dol.uploads.DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXPIRES_IN *= 900*

long enough to pick a file, short enough to
not be a standing upload credential.

* **Type:**
  Default form lifetime (seconds)

### *class* s3dol.uploads.DailyByteBudget(limit_bytes, \*, ledger=None, today=<function DailyByteBudget.<lambda>>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A per-day byte budget (one instance per tenant); call it to reserve.

`ledger` is any `MutableMapping[str, int]` (default: in-memory) keyed
by day, so persistence is a one-argument swap (a `dol` store, a file…).
`today` is the clock seam. Reservation is optimistic (the *maximum* the
form allows), and a form holds exactly one key, so re-posting cannot multiply the budget.

### *class* s3dol.uploads.PresignedUpload(url, fields=dict(), key='', key_prefix='', max_bytes=0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What the browser needs: POST `fields` + a `file` part to `url`.

### *exception* s3dol.uploads.UploadBudgetExceeded

Bases: [`S3Error`](_autosummary/s3dol.errors.html.md#s3dol.errors.S3Error)

The tenant’s byte budget cannot cover this upload; no form was signed.

### s3dol.uploads.presigned_upload(store, , key_prefix, max_bytes, content_type, min_bytes=0, expires_in=900, budget=None)

A presigned POST form for ONE new object under `key_prefix`.

`content_type` is required: pass the one type to accept, or `None` to
explicitly accept any (then a holder can store `text/html`: do not serve
such objects from a trusted origin).

`key_prefix` must end with the store’s delimiter (`tenant-7/` cannot
match `tenant-77/`) and is in the *store’s* key space (the store’s own
prefix is prepended, like every other s3dol key). The object key is
server-generated (`PresignedUpload.key`). Returns `None` for an
anonymous store (no signing capability, as [`s3dol.urls()`](_autosummary/s3dol.html.md#s3dol.urls) does).

Raises `ConfigurationError` for a bad prefix, size range or
`expires_in`, and [`UploadBudgetExceeded`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.UploadBudgetExceeded) if `budget` refuses.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`PresignedUpload`](_autosummary/s3dol.uploads.html.md#s3dol.uploads.PresignedUpload)]


# _autosummary/s3dol.values.html.md

# s3dol.values

Value refs and the write domain (ADR-0005).

The write domain is a small, closed, explicitly-named union:

```default
BytesSource = bytes | bytearray | memoryview | BinaryIO | Filepath | Chunks | Streamable
```

`Filepath`/`Chunks`/`Streamable` are tiny frozen dataclasses — value
*refs*, not values (h5py’s `SoftLink`/`ExternalLink` are the precedent:
purpose-built objects meaning “the value is a reference to content elsewhere”,
assigned through an ordinary `__setitem__`).

The law that makes the asymmetric read/write types safe (ADR-0005 §3):

- **N1 (canonical form)**: `normalize: WriteDomain -> bytes` is total on
  `bytes | bytearray | memoryview | Filepath` and **one-shot** on
  `BinaryIO | Chunks | Streamable` — a stream ref is consumed by its first
  write; assigning the same ref twice is a documented error, not a second copy.
- **N3 (the honest invariant)**: `s[k] = v  =>  s[k] == normalize(v)` — for
  the re-readable half.

`str` is rejected, loudly, on **decidability** (§2): `s['config'] = '{"a":1}'`
and `s['video'] = '/tmp/big.mp4'` are both overwhelmingly plausible, and any
rule distinguishing them is a latent data-corruption bug. One word —
`Filepath(p)` — removes the ambiguity. Bare `os.PathLike` is rejected too:
accepting it while rejecting `str` would be a confusing half-rule.

```pycon
>>> reject_str_value('{"a": 1}')
Traceback (most recent call last):
...
TypeError: ...
```

| [`reject_str_value`](_autosummary/s3dol.values.html.md#s3dol.values.reject_str_value)(v) | The one error message for the `str` ambiguity (ADR-0005 §2).         |

The static write domain (`BinaryIO` is for mypy; runtime dispatch uses

alias of [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes) | [`bytearray`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytearray) | [`memoryview`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#memoryview) | [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO) | [`Filepath`](_autosummary/s3dol.values.html.md#s3dol.values.Filepath) | [`Chunks`](_autosummary/s3dol.values.html.md#s3dol.values.Chunks) | [`Streamable`](_autosummary/s3dol.values.html.md#s3dol.values.Streamable)

### *class* s3dol.values.Chunks(chunks, consumed=list())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The value is the concatenation of an iterable of `bytes` chunks.
**One-shot** unless the iterable is re-iterable (a list is; a generator is
not — and a consumed generator writes `b''`, which is why assigning the
same one-shot ref twice is a documented error).

### *class* s3dol.values.Filepath(path)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The value *is the content of this file*. Re-readable (N1-total).

### *class* s3dol.values.Streamable(open_stream)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The value is whatever a zero-arg factory’s stream yields — for sources
that must be (re)opened at write time, e.g. an HTTP download. The factory
is called once per write, so unlike [`Chunks`](_autosummary/s3dol.values.html.md#s3dol.values.Chunks) this ref IS safely
re-writable (each write gets a fresh stream).

### s3dol.values.as_fileobj(v)

A binary file object for any member of the write domain.

`functools.singledispatch`: the union is open for extension (users
register their own ref types) and closed for modification. Everything
non-`bytes` routes through `upload_fileobj` downstream, so seekability
is s3transfer’s problem.

# _autosummary/s3dol.writes.html.md

# s3dol.writes

Write strategies (ADR-0005 §5): how `s[k] = v` reaches the wire.

A strategy is a callable `(client, bucket, key, value) -> None`, injected at
store construction — `__setitem__` stays `__setitem__`; *how* it uploads is
a constructor parameter. This is the answer to “infra-specific optimisation
without polluting the interface”: multipart is *transport*, not storage-model.

Strategies are frozen dataclasses, not closures, because every s3dol store
must pickle (ADR-0008 §6 / ADR-0012 D1) and a store carries its strategy.

Every non-`bytes` source routes through `upload_fileobj`/`TransferManager`,
never `PutObject` — so seekability is s3transfer’s problem, and the size
threshold is never consulted for a non-seekable source (where it is undecidable
anyway). Note `io.UnsupportedOperation` and botocore’s
`UnseekableStreamError` raise *before the request is built*, so they reach the
caller directly (they are not `ClientError``s and the error seam does not —
and must not — convert them to ``KeyError`).

```pycon
>>> strategy = transfer_writes(multipart_threshold=16 * 2**20)
>>> import pickle; pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(strategy)) == strategy
True
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_MULTIPART_THRESHOLD`](_autosummary/s3dol.writes.html.md#s3dol.writes.DEFAULT_MULTIPART_THRESHOLD)   | boto3's own default multipart threshold (8 MiB).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TransferWrites`](_autosummary/s3dol.writes.html.md#s3dol.writes.TransferWrites)([multipart_threshold, ...]) | The default: small in-memory values take a single `PutObject`; file objects and refs go through `upload_fileobj` (which goes multipart above the threshold, transparently). |

### *class* s3dol.writes.SimpleWrites

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Everything through a single `PutObject` — refs are materialised in

### *class* s3dol.writes.TransferWrites(multipart_threshold=8388608, multipart_chunksize=8388608, max_concurrency=10, use_threads=True)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The default: small in-memory values take a single `PutObject`; file
objects and refs go through `upload_fileobj` (which goes multipart above
the threshold, transparently). The overhead on small objects is one branch.

Providers that cap multipart parts (Scaleway: 1000 — see the preset’s
`Capabilities.max_multipart_parts`) may need a larger
`multipart_chunksize` for very large objects: parts ≈ size / chunksize.
